Exponential window-position weighting, w_j=exp[−λ(L−j)], emphasizes prediction targets near each sampled window’s end. It primarily redistributes supervision toward positions with longer available context; an old interaction can receive maximum weight when it ends a window. Absolute interaction recency instead uses distance from the user’s latest training interaction, exp[−λ(T_u−t)], while elapsed-time weighting uses timestamp age, exp[−γ(τ_ref−τ_t)]. These coincide with window weighting only under particular sampling/reference choices; irregular activity separates event distance from clock time. Thus, interpreting window weighting as removing stale preferences requires evidence beyond improved validation accuracy.

Closest evidence: [Petrov and Macdonald’s RSS study](https://arxiv.org/abs/2207.02643) compares training objectives and losses with fixed architectures, including GRU4Rec, and studies exponential target sampling. Results support the importance of supervision selection, but RSS also removes sampled targets and changes the prediction task; it does not isolate weighted next-item losses. Separately, [Recency Dropout](https://arxiv.org/abs/2201.11016) uses simulations and Jacobian analysis to investigate recurrent forgetting, supporting a distinct mechanism: sensitivity to earlier inputs rather than the weight assigned to prediction targets.

Recommended controlled ablations—not established results for this benchmark: compare uniform, window-position, absolute-event-recency, and timestamp-age weights on identical sampled windows, negatives, architecture, initialization, and update budgets. Cross weighting with window length and state reset/carry; measure lag-dependent input sensitivity to diagnose forgetting. Cross each with per-user normalization, mean_u[Σ_t w_utℓ_ut/Σ_t w_ut], versus pooled transition normalization, Σ_ut w_utℓ_ut/Σ_ut w_ut; the latter gives users influence proportional to their total sampled weight. Match overall loss scale and report effective target exposure by age, position, and history length. Timestamp permutation preserving interaction order tests whether gains require real elapsed time.
